decisions.diagnosis: Direction 869 recorded 871 bikes in an hour (519 in one 15-minute slot) while every adjoining zone that those riders must pass through recorded 0-9; a tracking artefact multiplied counts and the true value cannot be recovered.
Both directions at 328 jumped to 75-290 bikes per slot for 45 minutes while every adjoining zone stayed at normal levels; a tracking artefact multiplied counts and the true value cannot be recovered.

Both directions of the Margaret St zone fell to about 5% of their level for six weeks and then recovered, while every other zone was normal; this could be a zone that lost detection (occlusion) or a real closure of Margaret St.
decisions.evidence: 738/809 ~70-150 bikes/day before 2026-01-19 and after 2026-03-04, 1-17/day between; other zones unchanged.

decisions.diagnosis: Curtin Pl rose from ~2 bikes/day to ~170-190/day per direction over two weeks from mid June 2026, with a strong lunchtime peak in both directions; it may be a real new flow (e.g. delivery riders) or a zone reconfiguration.
decisions.evidence: 746/929 weekly ~10 through early June 2026, ~1150-1500/week from July; hourly peak 12-13h ~35-40/h each direction; IN and OUT balanced.

decisions.diagnosis: Both directions at George St (W) south of Margaret St ran 3-20 times their usual level all day for four weekdays, including late evening, while other zones were normal; could be a diversion onto the footpath or a detection artefact.
Both directions at 326 ran 3-8 times their usual level for five days, all day, while other zones were normal; could be a diversion or a detection artefact.

After the camera restarted in August 2024 both George St (E) north directions read far lower than before the outage (792 about a fifth), while most other zones matched their pre-outage levels; the zone may have been redrawn.

proposals: Backlog slots: camera 278 twice dumped a whole outage into one slot (2025-12-18 03:00 after a 6.5 h gap, and 2026-02-01 09:30 after ~32 h absent from 2026-01-31 01:00). Weekly totals are right as published because each dump falls in the same week, but a fix that spreads a dump slot back over the empty slots it covers, in proportion to the direction's usual profile, would also make the daily and 15-minute views right.

counter_days: pinned the start and end of the 2024 zero period and the partial recommissioning day
zeros(counter=True): listed every camera-wide outage, including short ones (2023-09-20, 2023-11-10) that weekly views hide
slots pivoted by direction: separated single-zone tracking artefacts (2026-02-13, 2026-08-14) from backlog dumps (2026-02-01 09:30) by comparing adjoining zones
hourly: showed the lunchtime profile of the new Curtin Pl flow
monthly across neighbours: the Pitt/King camera also stepped up ~2.3x in late 2024, supporting separate series
not_useful: doubled/duplicates: nothing to find on a single-record camera feed
spikes: 554 rows at usual=0 for many low-volume zones; needed heavy aggregation to use
improve: spikes: add a column with what the other zones of the same camera did in the same slots, so single-zone artefacts stand out from real group rides
zeros: flag whether the stretch ends in a slot far above usual (a backlog dump) so outages that were recovered are distinguishable from lost ones
overview: a wide per-month view (like weekly wide) would save a pivot for cameras with many zones

summary: Camera 278 at George St / Margaret St / Curtin Pl published zeros from 2024-05-11 to 2024-08-29 and had several shorter camera-wide outages and single-zone tracking artefacts, all set missing; since recommissioning in Nov 2025 the feed omits zero slots, so it is zero-filled. After its 14-month gap the camera reads 2-3 times higher with a different IN/OUT balance, so each direction is split into a 2023-2024 and a 2025+ series, and the 2022 trial counter 250 stays separate. Margaret St's six-week collapse in early 2026, Curtin Pl's large rise from June 2026 and multi-day surges at 326 are flagged uncertain.
